title: Stupid idea: “Best Slop on Earth” – a 3 prompt game challenge
author: Phllori
selftext:
I had a stupid idea and I'm curious if anyone here would actually be interested in doing this.

**Best Slop on Earth.**

The idea is simple:

You have to make a complete game using AI, but you get **exactly 3 prompts**.

Not up to 3.

Not 1.

Not 2.

**Exactly 3.**

You can use them however you want. One giant prompt to build the whole game? Fine. One for code, one for graphics and one for sound? Fine. Waste your second prompt asking the AI to make the main character's hat bigger? Also fine. That's your problem.

AI agents and tool calls would be allowed. If you tell an agent to build the whole game, test it and fix its own mistakes, it can do that.

The important part is that **the human only gets 3 inputs.**

Everything creative in the final game should be AI-generated: code, graphics, 3D models, music, sounds, text, etc. Manual work should basically be limited to putting things together, importing/exporting files and getting the build running.

And there would be one important requirement:

**You have to submit the complete chat log.**

  


So everyone can see the three prompts you used and what happened between you and the AI. No secret fourth *“please fix this fucking thing”* prompt.

I was thinking maybe give everyone one week, then put all finished games into one voting thread here. Each game gets its own comment and the Reddit upvotes decide the winner.

The prize?

Absolutely nothing.

Except the completely meaningless but prestigious title:

**🏆 BEST SLOP ON EARTH 2026**

Maybe a terrible AI-generated golden trophy PNG to go with it.

  


I actually think it could be a fun little experiment too. If everyone only gets three prompts, the interesting part becomes less *“who can program/model/etc. the best?”* and more *“who can turn an idea into something good with three instructions?”*

Would anyone here actually participate if we did this?

replies.author: Phllori
replies.body: What exactly do you want to copy and paste if there’s no genre and no setting? That’s precisely what makes it interesting... of course it’s possible, but what’s the result?

comments.body: I’m more or less doing this. I give the same prompt over and over and the game builds itself. I think I will market it as the world’s first SaaS- slop as a service - live game.

comments.author: ActuallyAdasi
comments.body:
Just want to point out that harnesses make the 3 prompt limit completely arbitrary and meaningless. One prompt from Claude code for example will turn into a bunch of other prompts and several model invocations.

A more interesting competition would be to have a finite number of model invocations. Ties are broken by who used less tokens. Gotta show the log for full credit.

replies.author: Phllori
replies.body:
That’s actually a good point, but I think that’s a different challenge. My goal isn't really to limit the number of model calls or tokens. The idea is rather to restrict the user to exactly three inputs and then see what the AI—or the agent—makes of them. If Claude generates 50 internal prompts from that, I’m totally fine with it. Let it do the heavy lifting. :D



But usually, the result is still rubbish, and then you end up needing a few more prompts to fix it anyway.
